correctness.rationale: The positive trace-norm Gram sum follows from explicit Cesaro matrix products. The lower bound uses an n-dimensional subspace with finite-difference inverse norm at most 2 and coefficients at least 1/(12n^3). The upper bound imposes fewer than 7n zero-sum constraints on exponentially scaled blocks of length at most ceil(2^(3j/2)), giving Rayleigh quotient <= 4/n^3; the tail starts beyond n^3. Courant-Fischer and comparison of p-series supply the exact Schatten threshold. Independent exact-rational auxiliary finite checks passed.
